OUTCAST.SAVED: Saved. The uplinks are being set up.
OUTCAST.ADVANCED_DESC: The encoding, the bitrate, the sample rate and the channels as you set them; the settings above are then not used. The plugin refuses nothing: a server or the encoder that cannot take a value says so in the status.
OUTCAST.BITRATE_DESC: kbit/s, any value. Commonly 128 for MP3 and AAC, 64 to 96 for Opus. Nothing for FLAC and WAV.
OUTCAST.RATE_DESC: Hz, any value, or 0 for the player's own rate. A rate that is set gives one continuous stream at that rate whatever the player plays, converted in the core without loss; 0 follows the player and the stream starts anew at each change.
OUTCAST.CHANNELS_DESC: Stereo, mono, or the player's own.
OUTCAST.ICE_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: The mount stays up with silence while the player pauses or stops, from the moment the uplink is on; off, the server sees the stream come and go with the player.
OUTCAST.LAN_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: The stream goes on with silence while the player pauses or stops, so a listener stays connected; off, it ends with the player.
OUTCAST.ICE_SECTION_DESC: Whatever the player plays, from any service, sent to an Icecast server (also AzuraCast, Zeno, Live365, Radio.co and most hosted radio). If the server goes away the stream reconnects by itself; playback on this player is never affected. The title the player shows goes with it.
OUTCAST.ICE_SECTION_MORE_DESC: A second (or third) destination, with its own settings and status; each is its own encoder and connection, and one failing never stops another.
OUTCAST.ICE_ENABLE_DESC: Send the stream to an Icecast server.
OUTCAST.ICE_HOST_DESC: The host name or IP address of the Icecast server.
OUTCAST.ICE_PORT_DESC: The port the server listens on, usually 8000. For SHOUTcast the server's own port: the source connects one above it, as SHOUTcast expects.
OUTCAST.ICE_PROTOCOL_DESC: Icecast 2 for Icecast and the hosts built on it; SHOUTcast for a SHOUTcast DNAS, version 1 or version 2 in its legacy mode.
OUTCAST.ICE_MOUNT_DESC: Icecast 2 servers: the path the stream is published under, for example /volumio.mp3. Must start with /.
OUTCAST.ICE_STREAM_ID_DESC: SHOUTcast servers: 1 for a v1 server or the first stream of a v2 one; the stream's number on a v2 server with several.
OUTCAST.ICE_USER_DESC: Icecast 2 servers: the source user name on the server, usually source.
OUTCAST.ICE_PASSWORD_DESC: The server's source password for this mount.
OUTCAST.ICE_PRESET_DESC: What a server of this kind commonly takes. Internet radio mostly runs MP3 at 128 kbit/s and 44.1 kHz; AAC gives the same at a lower bitrate; an Icecast server takes any of them, a SHOUTcast DNAS takes MP3 and AAC. Anything else under Advanced.
OUTCAST.ICE_CODEC_DESC: What the encoder can make. MP3 and AAC carry the title through the server; Opus and Ogg Vorbis carry it in the stream; FLAC goes in Ogg. The server refuses what it does not take.
OUTCAST.ICE_MORE_DESC: What the server shows about the stream.
OUTCAST.ICE_URL_DESC: A web address the server announces.
OUTCAST.ICE_PUBLIC_DESC: Let the server list the stream in public directories.
OUTCAST.LAN_SECTION_DESC: The player serves what it plays as a stream any player on the network can open at http://<player address>:<port>/ . Titles are shown by players that ask for them.
OUTCAST.LAN_ENABLE_DESC: Serve the stream from this player.
OUTCAST.LAN_PORT_DESC: The port the stream is served on (1 to 65535). Not one the player uses already.
OUTCAST.LAN_PRESET_DESC: What players on the network commonly take: MP3 and AAC play everywhere, Opus and Ogg Vorbis carry titles in the stream, FLAC is lossless. Anything else under Advanced.
OUTCAST.LAN_CODEC_DESC: MP3 and AAC play everywhere; Opus and Ogg Vorbis carry titles in the stream; FLAC is lossless and needs more bandwidth.
OUTCAST.LAN_MAX_DESC: How many players may listen at once (1 to 64).
OUTCAST.REC_SECTION_DESC: Whatever the player plays, written to files in a folder of the player, a file per track or one per stream.
OUTCAST.REC_FOLDER_DESC: Where the files go. Under /data/INTERNAL they are on the player's own storage and reachable over the network share; a mounted NAS folder works too.
OUTCAST.REC_PRESET_DESC: FLAC as played keeps every bit of what the player plays at its own rate; the others for smaller files or a fixed rate. Anything else under Advanced.
OUTCAST.REC_CODEC_DESC: FLAC and WAV are lossless; the others are smaller.
OUTCAST.REC_BITRATE_DESC: kbit/s, any value, for MP3, AAC, Opus and Ogg Vorbis. Nothing for FLAC and WAV.
OUTCAST.REC_RATE_DESC: Hz, any value, or 0 for the player's own rate, nothing resampled.
OUTCAST.REC_SPLIT_DESC: A file per track starts a new file at every title the player shows; one per stream runs from play to stop.
OUTCAST.REC_TITLE_IN_NAME_DESC: Name each file by the moment it begins and the title the player shows.
OUTCAST.SRT_SECTION_DESC: Whatever the player plays, sent as an MPEG transport stream over SRT to a listener: a production switcher, a broadcast encoder, a gateway, a server. This player calls; the listener's own settings decide what it takes. If the link goes away it is made again by itself; playback here is never affected.
OUTCAST.SRT_ENABLE_DESC: Send the stream to an SRT listener.
OUTCAST.SRT_HOST_DESC: The host name or IP address of the SRT listener.
OUTCAST.SRT_PORT_DESC: The UDP port the listener waits on.
OUTCAST.SRT_STREAM_ID_DESC: The stream id the listener asks for, if it asks for one; empty otherwise.
OUTCAST.SRT_PASSPHRASE_DESC: The passphrase for an encrypted link, 10 to 79 characters, the same as the listener's; empty for no encryption.
OUTCAST.SRT_LATENCY_DESC: Milliseconds the link may hold a packet to recover a lost one; 120 on a LAN, more over the internet, at least twice the round trip.
OUTCAST.SRT_PRESET_DESC: What receivers of a transport stream commonly take: AAC at 128 kbit/s and 48 kHz for most; MP2 where the receiver is a broadcast chain. Anything else under Advanced.
OUTCAST.SRT_CODEC_DESC: What the encoder can put in a transport stream. The receiver refuses what it does not take.
OUTCAST.SRT_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: The link stays up with silence while the player pauses or stops, from the moment the uplink is on; off, the link follows the player.
OUTCAST.RTMP_SECTION_DESC: Publish the stream to an RTMP ingest: a streaming platform, a media server or a CDN. The address and the stream key come from the platform's live settings.
OUTCAST.RTMP_ENABLE_DESC: Publish to the RTMP address below and reconnect when the link breaks.
OUTCAST.RTMP_URL_DESC: rtmp://host[:port]/application, or rtmps:// for a server behind TLS, as the platform gives it.
OUTCAST.RTMP_KEY_DESC: The key or stream name the platform issues; it is the stream's password and stays hidden.
OUTCAST.RTMP_CA_FILE_DESC: For rtmps:// to a server whose certificate is from a private authority: the path of that authority's PEM file on the player. Empty trusts the public authorities alone.
OUTCAST.RTMP_PRESET_DESC: What RTMP platforms commonly take: AAC at 44.1 kHz. Switch Advanced on to set every value yourself.
OUTCAST.RTMP_CODEC_DESC: AAC is what nearly every RTMP ingest takes; MP3 for servers that accept it.
OUTCAST.RTMP_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: Stay published while the player is stopped or paused, sending silence; off closes the connection and reopens it on play.
OUTCAST.TS_SECTION_DESC: Send the stream as an MPEG transport stream to a decoder, an encoder input or a broadcast gateway, over TCP or UDP.
OUTCAST.TS_ENABLE_DESC: Connect to the address below (TCP) or send datagrams to it (UDP) and reconnect when the link breaks.
OUTCAST.TS_TRANSPORT_DESC: TCP connects to a listener and notices when it is gone; UDP sends datagrams to a host or a multicast group and cannot tell.
OUTCAST.TS_HOST_DESC: The receiver's name or address; for UDP a multicast group address (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255) is allowed.
OUTCAST.TS_PORT_DESC: The receiver's port; 5004 is the common choice.
OUTCAST.TS_TTL_DESC: For UDP multicast only: how many routers the datagrams may cross; 1 keeps them on this network.
OUTCAST.TS_PRESET_DESC: What transport-stream receivers commonly take: AAC or MP2 at 48 kHz. Switch Advanced on to set every value yourself.
OUTCAST.TS_CODEC_DESC: AAC and MP2 are what broadcast decoders take; MP3 and Opus for receivers that accept them.
OUTCAST.TS_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: Keep sending while the player is stopped or paused, with silence; off stops sending and starts again on play.
OUTCAST.HLS_SECTION_DESC: The stream as HTTP Live Streaming: segments of a few seconds and a playlist, as a browser, a phone, a smart speaker and a CDN take it. Served from the player's memory on a port of its own, and put on your own origin for the world.
OUTCAST.HLS_ENABLE_DESC: Cut the stream into segments and keep a playlist of the latest.
OUTCAST.HLS_NAME_DESC: The playlist is <name>.m3u8 and the segments <name>-<number>; letters, digits, dash and underscore.
OUTCAST.HLS_FORM_DESC: Packed audio (AAC or MP3 frames with an ID3 tag) is what radio CDNs serve and every HLS player takes. Fragmented MP4 (CMAF) is what Apple recommends, takes FLAC for lossless HLS and Opus, and is what DASH needs.
OUTCAST.HLS_DASH_DESC: A DASH manifest (<name>.mpd) beside the playlist, from the same segments, for players that take DASH rather than HLS.
OUTCAST.HLS_PRESET_DESC: What HLS players commonly take: AAC at 48 kHz; MP3 for the oldest players. Switch Advanced on to set every value yourself.
OUTCAST.HLS_CODEC_DESC: AAC plays everywhere HLS does; MP3 as packed audio plays on most; FLAC (lossless) and Opus need fragmented MP4, Opus for DASH players.
OUTCAST.HLS_SEGMENT_DESC: How long each segment is meant to be, 1 to 30 seconds; 4 is the common choice, longer for a CDN that prefers fewer files.
OUTCAST.HLS_WINDOW_DESC: How many of the latest segments the playlist names, 3 to 60; 6 is the common choice.
OUTCAST.HLS_SERVE_DESC: The playlist and the segments at http://<player>:<port>/<name>.m3u8, from memory, for anything on the network.
OUTCAST.HLS_PORT_DESC: The port the player serves HLS on; 8010 unless taken.
OUTCAST.HLS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_DESC: How many connections the player's HLS server holds at once, 1 to 1000; more are refused at once (503), so a flood never grows without bound. 64 unless set.
OUTCAST.HLS_KEEP_ALIVE_DESC: Keep cutting segments of silence while the player is stopped or paused, so a listener's player keeps going; off lets the playlist stand still.
OUTCAST.HLS_ORIGIN_DESC: Where the files go beyond the player: none, or an HTTP origin that takes PUT and DELETE (a WebDAV folder, a CDN's ingest, a media server's HTTP origin).
OUTCAST.HLS_ORIGIN_URL_DESC: The folder the files go in: http://host/path/ or https://host/path/.
OUTCAST.HLS_ORIGIN_USER_DESC: For an origin that asks for basic authentication; empty for none.
OUTCAST.HLS_ORIGIN_PASSWORD_DESC: The user's password; it stays hidden.
OUTCAST.HLS_CA_FILE_DESC: For https:// to an origin whose certificate is from a private authority: the path of that authority's PEM file on the player. Empty trusts the public authorities alone.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_ENDPOINT_DESC: The storage's address: https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com for AWS, https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com for Cloudflare R2, https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com for Backblaze B2, or your own server.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_BUCKET_DESC: The bucket the files go in; it must exist, and a CDN or a public-read policy must serve it.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_PREFIX_DESC: A path inside the bucket the files go under, such as radio/live; empty for the bucket's root.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_REGION_DESC: The region the signature is made for: the bucket's AWS region, auto for Cloudflare R2, the region in the endpoint for Backblaze B2, us-east-1 for most others.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_ACCESS_KEY_DESC: The key id of a user allowed to put and delete objects in the bucket.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_SECRET_KEY_DESC: The key's secret; it stays hidden.
OUTCAST.HLS_S3_PATH_STYLE_DESC: On: endpoint/bucket/…, what Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 and most servers take. Off: bucket.endpoint/…, AWS's own way.
OUTCAST.DJ_SECTION_DESC: The programme as blocks over the day: at each block's start the player is told what to play, a playlist on random or in order, a web radio, or left to its own queue, at the end of the track playing or on the clock. The blocks are set on the programme page.
OUTCAST.DJ_ENABLE_DESC: On, the programme drives the player. Off, nothing of the player's is touched. A queue changed by hand makes DJ mode stand back until the next block.
OUTCAST.DJ_OPEN_DESC: The programme page inside Volumio's own page with its arrow back: the blocks, their sources, what is on now and what comes next.
OUTCAST.DJ_OPEN_TAB: Open the programme in a new tab
OUTCAST.DJ_OPEN_TAB_DESC: The same page in a tab of its own. Its address:
OUTCAST.MON_SECTION_DESC: The status watches the programme's level from the tap and says when there has been dead air: the player playing silence or playing nothing, for longer than the time set.
OUTCAST.MON_ENABLE_DESC: Say in the status when the programme has gone silent.
OUTCAST.MON_LEVEL_DESC: dBFS; the programme below it counts as silent. -60 is the usual floor.
OUTCAST.MON_SECONDS_DESC: Seconds of silence before the status says dead air; 0 never.
OUTCAST.MON_DASHBOARD_DESC: A page of the core's own on a port of the player, for watching the programme, the level, dead air and every uplink from anything on the network, a second at a time. The Status section has the button that opens it.
OUTCAST.MON_DASHBOARD_PORT_DESC: The port the dashboard is served on; 8020 unless taken.
OUTCAST.MON_DASHBOARD_HOST_DESC: How browsers reach this player. Empty uses the address found on the player's own network interface, which works where .local names do not resolve. Enter a host name or an IP address of your own when the player is reached another way (a name you keep, another interface, a proxy).
OUTCAST.STATUS_DASHBOARD_DESC: The live page in this window, inside Volumio's own page with its arrow back: the programme, the level, dead air and every uplink, updated every second.
OUTCAST.STATUS_DASHBOARD_TAB: Open the dashboard in a new tab
OUTCAST.STATUS_DASHBOARD_TAB_DESC: The same page in a tab of its own, for a second screen or another device. Its address:
OUTCAST.STATUS_SECTION_DESC: What the player is playing as the tap sees it, and the state of every uplink.
OUTCAST.STATUS_PLAYING: Playing: {{rate}} Hz, {{channels}} channels, {{format}}; {{segments}} streams so far, {{mb}} MB carried.
OUTCAST.STATUS_DEAD_AIR: Dead air: {{seconds}} s below the level.
OUTCAST.STATUS_SINCE: Since {{time}}: {{dead}} dead air, {{reconnects}} reconnects, {{errors}} errors, {{overs}} overs.
OUTCAST.STATUS_HLS_SEGMENTS: {{segments}} segments cut, {{pending}} waiting for the origin
OUTCAST.STATUS_HLS_REFUSED: {{refused}} requests refused at the connection limit
OUTCAST.STATUS_TAP_READY: The tap is in the audio chain.
OUTCAST.STATUS_TAP_FAILED: The tap is not in the audio chain: {{error}}
OUTCAST.STATUS_TAP_LOST: The tap was taken out of the audio chain by a later change; disable and enable the plugin to put it back.
OUTCAST.STATUS_TAP_SHARED: The tap is served by another plugin's copy of the same library ({{path}}).
OUTCAST.STATUS_TAP_FOREIGN: The tap is served by another plugin's library ({{path}}), not the same build as this plugin's; the core's ring reader decides whether it fits.
OUTCAST.ERR_LIBRARY: The tap library for this player's architecture is missing from the plugin.
OUTCAST.ERR_PREFLIGHT: The player's ALSA could not load the tap: {{error}}
OUTCAST.ERR_CHAIN: The audio chain did not take the tap; the change was taken back: {{error}}
OUTCAST.ERR_CORE: The core could not be started: {{error}}
OUTCAST.ERR_PORT: {{field}} must be a number from 1 to 65535.
OUTCAST.ERR_DASHBOARD_HOST: The dashboard address must be a host name or an IP address, without http:// or a port.
OUTCAST.ERR_MOUNT: The mount point must start with / and hold no spaces.
OUTCAST.ERR_PASSPHRASE: The passphrase must be 10 to 79 characters, or empty.
OUTCAST.ERR_RTMP_URL: The ingest address must look like rtmp://host/application.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_NOWHERE: HLS must be served on the player, go to an origin, or both.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_ORIGIN_URL: The origin address must look like http://host/path/ or https://host/path/.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_PACKED_CODEC: Packed audio takes AAC or MP3; choose fragmented MP4 for FLAC or Opus.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_S3_ENDPOINT: The endpoint must look like https://host/.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_S3_BUCKET: The bucket name must be lower-case letters, digits, dots and dashes.
OUTCAST.ERR_HLS_S3_KEYS: An access key and a secret key are needed.
OUTCAST.ERR_TEXT: {{field}} must hold no quotation marks or line breaks.
OUTCAST.ERR_FOLDER: The folder must be an absolute path, starting with /.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_SHAPE: The programme did not arrive whole.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_START: Every block needs a start time as HH:MM.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_SAME_START: Two blocks start at the same time.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_NAME: A block's name must hold no quotation marks or line breaks.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_SOURCE: A block's source must be the player's queue, a playlist or a web radio.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_PLAYLIST: A playlist block needs the playlist's name.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_URI: A web radio block needs the stream's address, http:// or https://.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_INSERT_FILE: An insert needs a WAV file from the jingles folder.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_INSERT_WHEN: An insert plays every hour, every so many tracks, or at a block's start.
OUTCAST.ERR_DJ_INSERT_NUMBER: An insert's minute must be 0 to 59, its track count 1 or more, and its level 0 to −60 dB.
OUTCAST.ERR_SAVE: The settings could not be saved: {{error}}
